title: Unemployment Benefit Claims — Computing the Value of a Waiting Week
content:
The value of a waiting week on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record is the amount the week would have paid. The week valued is the latest week certified on the claim, read by week ending date, and its figures are those on its certification.

## Definition

The waiting-week value is the weekly benefit amount plus the dependency allowance, less the earnings deduction and less the other-pay deduction, rounded down to the whole dollar and never below zero.

- **Earnings disregard:** the program's disregard share of the weekly benefit amount, rounded to the cent.
- **Earnings deduction:** every dollar of earnings above the disregard.
- **Dependency allowance:** counted in full.
- **Other-pay deduction:** vacation or holiday pay in full; an employer-funded pension at the program's pension offset share; a claimant-contributed pension at the program's claimant-contributed share; each rounded to the cent. Severance pay is not deducted.
- Both deductions are subtracted from the weekly benefit amount plus the allowance in one step before rounding down.

## Weeks not valued

- A week whose hours reach the program's full-time hours threshold does not serve and is not valued.
- No week is valued once the claim carries its program's waiting week count of waiting-week entries.

## Worked example (hypothetical week, Regular State Unemployment Insurance figures)

Weekly benefit amount 346.00, dependency allowance 15.00; the week reports 200.00 of earnings and 12.0 hours, with holiday pay of 40.00; the claim carries no waiting-week entry.

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| Disregard: 0.30 times 346.00 | 103.80 |
| Earnings deduction: 200.00 less 103.80 | 96.20 |
| Other-pay deduction: holiday pay in full | 40.00 |
| 346.00 plus 15.00, less 96.20 and 40.00 | 224.80 |
| Waiting-week value, rounded down | 224.00 |

The same week reporting 32.0 hours, under a 32-hour threshold, is not valued.
